q-132303.name: Question 1
q-132303.problem: Use trial and error to find the solutions, if any, to the congruence $4x≡5\,(\text{mod}\,8).$
q-132303.worked_solution:
Since the modulus $n=8$ is fairly small, we can solve the congruence by trial and error. 

Substituting $x=0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7$ into the equation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}4\cdot 0 & ≡0≢5 &  & (\text{mod}\,8) &  & \times  \\ 4\cdot 1 & ≡4≢5 &  & (\text{mod}\,8) &  & \times  \\ 4\cdot 2 & ≡0≢5 &  & (\text{mod}\,8) &  & \times  \\ 4\cdot 3 & ≡4≢5 &  & (\text{mod}\,8) &  & \times  \\ 4\cdot 4 & ≡0≢5 &  & (\text{mod}\,8) &  & \times  \\ 4\cdot 5 & ≡4≢5 &  & (\text{mod}\,8) &  & \times  \\ 4\cdot 6 & ≡0≢5 &  & (\text{mod}\,8) &  & \times  \\ 4\cdot 7 & ≡4≢5 &  & (\text{mod}\,8) &  & \times \end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, our congruence does not have any solutions.

$$
